say: Many women undervalue what they do. For example, Mercy has sold foodstuff at a market in Ibadan for eight years, and has been treasurer of her women's association for three. Her LinkedIn page was empty.
Now her first entry reads Owner, Mercy's Provisions, with about 150 regular customers. Her second reads Treasurer, recording contributions for 40 members in Google Sheets.
An NGO recruiter searching for record-keeping in Ibadan can now find her.
Phishing is when criminals pretend to be your bank, Google or even WODDI, to trick you into giving passwords, codes or money.
If you see even one of these red flags, stop. Press and hold a link to preview the real address without opening it.

panel.heading: Stop and check if you see these
items: Urgent threat or a prize
Sender address looks wrong
Link goes somewhere strange
Asks for PIN, password or code
Generic greeting, poor spelling

say: Your email can reset all your other passwords, so it needs the strongest one: a long passphrase that you use nowhere else.

panel.heading: Lock your accounts and act fast

cards.d: A long passphrase, different for your email. Never your name, birthday or 123456.
Turn it on in your Google Account Security tab. Save backup codes on paper at home.
Call your bank's official number at once. Change your email password and sign out other sessions.

say: Switch on 2-Step Verification in the Security tab of your Google Account. Then a criminal cannot get in without your phone, even with your password. Set a WhatsApp PIN too.

say: If you clicked or shared details, act immediately. Call your bank's official number to block the card or account. Change your email password from a safe device, and warn your contacts.
And remember, real employers never ask you to pay to get a job.

say: To remember. Search yourself privately. Stay consistent everywhere. Count all your work, with numbers. Never give your PIN, password or OTP. And turn on 2-Step Verification today.
